sum: A ten-day walk from the Tamakoshi road up the Rolwaling valley, through Simigaon and Beding to the summer village of Na and the glacial lake of Tsho Rolpa at 4,580 m.

guide.note: Rolwaling is a restricted area: the permit is issued only through a registered trekking agency, and you must walk with a licensed guide. Since March 2026 the permit can be issued to a single trekker, so you no longer need a second person in order to apply. A guide who knows the valley matters in practice too: they phone ahead to find out which lodges in Dongang, Beding and Na are open, which decides whether the trip is possible at all outside the main seasons.

access: A long day by road from Kathmandu: the Araniko Highway to the Sun Koshi, over the hills to Charikot, down to the Tamakoshi and north on the hydropower road through Singati to Chetchet. The section beyond Singati is rough and can close after heavy rain.

photo.a: The long, milky grey-green lake of Tsho Rolpa lies between steep rock walls and grey moraine, with a snow-covered peak at the head of the valley.
photo.c: Tsho Rolpa glacial lake in the Rolwaling valley, 4,580 m

includes: porter in most packages (the cheapest tiers leave one out)
lodge beds and three meals a day on the trek
bus or jeep from Kathmandu and back

permits.name: Gaurishankar Conservation Area Permit
permits.where: Online at NTNC's e-permit site or at the Tourist Service Centre in Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu. A permit issued at a trail checkpost costs double.

permits.name: Dolakha (Gaurishankar and Lamabagar) restricted area permit
permits.where: Department of Immigration in Kathmandu, through a registered trekking agency only.

transportText: Bus between Kathmandu and Dolakha district, each way
transportExtra: the local jeep on to Chetchet
tips: Bring all your cash from Kathmandu or Charikot. Nothing in the valley takes cards.
Carry a warm sleeping bag; lodge bedding is thin and sometimes shared.
Meals are vegetarian: by local custom no animal is killed in Rolwaling, so do not ask for meat.
Phone signal is patchy beyond Simigaon and often absent above Dongang. Agree check-in days with someone at home before you leave.
The restricted area permit is issued in Kathmandu against your passport and visa, so allow a working day there before you set off.

days.note: Leave early. The road is mostly sealed as far as Singati and rough beyond it. Chetchet is a handful of houses beside a waterfall, with very simple rooms; some groups climb on to Simigaon the same evening.

Cross the Tamakoshi on the suspension bridge and climb about 600 m of stone steps with no break to the village. It is short but steep, and hot by mid-morning. Use the afternoon to recover from the drive and walk up to the monastery for the view of Gaurishankar.

The trail climbs through the village to a shoulder, then stays in oak and rhododendron forest high above the Rolwaling gorge, with steep ups and downs and a tea shack or two on the way, before dropping to the river at Dongang. Leeches are common here in the wet months and into October.

A long climb beside the river through forest that thins to juniper and open hillside, with Beding appearing late in the day. You gain close to 900 m of sleeping height, more than is wise, and there is little to stop at in between. Walk slowly and drink often.
why: Sleeping altitude rises 690 m, well over the 500 m guideline even with a rest night next to it.

days.note: Stay put after yesterday's gain. Visit the monastery, then walk an hour or two up the hillside behind the village or along the valley toward Na, and come back for lunch. If you still have a headache tonight, do not go higher tomorrow.

A gentle morning up the widening valley past mani walls and yak pastures. Na is a scatter of stone houses on a broad flat; its lodges open only when the families are up for the season, so make sure yours is expecting you.

Follow the river flats for an hour, then climb the terminal moraine to the lake. Walk along the crest for the view down its length to the ice at the far end. Allow four to five hours for the round trip and keep off the loose inner slopes.
Downhill almost all day: two to three hours to Beding, then the long forest descent. You lose about 1,400 m, which is hard on the knees. Break the day at Beding if you have time in hand.

Back along the high forest trail above the gorge. It has nearly as much up as down, so do not expect a quick morning. Simigaon's lodges are the most comfortable of the trek and a good place for the last night.

days.t: Simigaon to Chetchet, drive to Kathmandu
days.note: About ninety minutes down the staircase to the bridge at Chetchet, where your jeep should be waiting, then the full day's drive back. If you are using public transport, plan on a night in Charikot.
